newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity halts skid amid shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity halts skid amid shortcovering.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Thursday on a shortcovering rally, and halted its skid this week due to mild weather in the West and increased generation from two key Western nuclear power units.
"It's a bit of shortcovering and people who are long trying to hold it up," said a Houston futures trader.
Revised outlooks of several forecasters calling for warmer-than-normal weather in West beginning next week also propelled the complex higher, market sources said.
July California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 95 cents at $18.09 a megawatt hour after hitting a session high at $18.70.
August COB finished up $1.26 at $22.42, near its intraday high at $22.50. September COB, the other active contract, edned up 98 cents at $22.12.
July Palo Verde (PV) settled up $1.06 at $28.05, trimming an $1.89 gain and partially filled a gap at $28.30-30.30.
August PV finished up $1.46 at $31.11. Deferred PV ended ended 75 cents to $1.00 higher.
The Diablo Canyon 1 and Palo Verde 3 nuclear power units continued to boost output as of early Thursday.
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1, located in Avila Beach, Calif., was operating at 48 percent of capacity as of early Thursday from 30 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday.

The 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3, located in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 80 percent of capacity and was holding at that level for instrument calibration from 45 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday.
Palo Verde 3 was taken off line Saturday due to a circuit problem.

Meterologists said temperatures in the Northwest would run near to slightly above normal into early next week, while those in the Southwest would average near to slightly below seasonal norms, dampening some air conditioning demand.
More supply and outlook of cooler weather in the Southwest held down physical electricity values in the West.
Firm, peak power prices for Friday at COB $13.50-14.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared with Wednesday's $12.50-14.00, while those at PV were assessed at $22.50-23.50 versus $22.00-24.00 Wednesday.
Market sources said today's rise in power futures would continue Friday.
"Technically, there's still more to go," said another Houston futures trader.
